confirmed.title: Pool-then-admission lock-order inversion can wedge the whole broker
confirmed.failure_scenario: The six metered db.rs wrappers (ack_at:175, ack_by_hash:231, seg_dlq_head:267, renew_lease:529, transaction:551, streams_cycle:1821) block on admission::lane_slot() while their caller already holds a checked-out deadpool client (handlers/data.rs:2397 held across db::ack_at at 2500 and db::ack_by_hash at 2614; fusion-ON fallback acquires at 2582 then holds across 2614; handle_lease_extend 2970->2982; handle_transaction 3321->3535; streams.rs:346->350). Every other admitted path takes the opposite order: slot first, then pool.get (handle_pop data.rs:612->615, hotlist data.rs:1344->1346, fusion.rs try_acquire->pool.get:1095, pop_fusion.rs:285->296, ack_fusion.rs:322->pool.get). Concrete wedge with defaults (DB_POOL_SIZE=160, budget ceiling min(128,160-16)=128): a burst of >=160 concurrent ack/renew/transaction/streams requests each checks out a connection at handler entry, draining the pool, then parks in lane_slot because the budget is exhausted by >=128 pop/push tasks that acquired slots and are now parked in pool.get on the empty pool. Slots are only released by Slot::drop (holders are stuck in pool.get) and connections only return when the ack handlers finish (stuck in acquire) -> circular wait. PoolConfig::new(cfg.pool_size) at db.rs:11 sets no deadpool timeouts, so pool.get waits forever; admission acquire has no timeout either; axum concurrency is unbounded. admission_pool_reserve=16 does not help: it only lowers the budget ceiling arithmetically, nothing reserves actual connections from the pool-first callers. Permanent, broker-wide deadlock; recoverable only by restart.
confirmed.why: CONFIRMED by reading the code. (1) All six db.rs wrappers (ack_at:175, ack_by_hash:231, seg_dlq_head:267, renew_lease:529, transaction:551, streams_cycle:1821) take a borrowed &deadpool_postgres::Client and internally await admission::lane_slot(), which parks on an untimed oneshot (admission.rs:340) when the budget is exhausted — so they block on admission while the caller's pool connection stays checked out. (2) The callers do hold connections across these calls exactly as claimed: handlers/data.rs handle_ack fusion-OFF pool.get at 2397 held across ack_at (2500) and ack_by_hash (2614); fusion-ON fallback pool.get at 2582 held across 2614; handle_lease_extend 2970→2982; handle_transaction pool.get→db::transaction; streams.rs pool.get→db::streams_cycle. (3) All admitted paths take the opposite order, holding the Slot across the pool.get await: handle_pop data.rs 614→615, hotlist 1344→1346, pop_fusion.rs 285→296, ack_fusion.rs 322→343, fusion.rs try_acquire→pool.get 1095. (4) No timeout anywhere breaks the cycle: PoolConfig::new(cfg.pool_size) (db.rs:11, deadpool-postgres 0.14.1) leaves default Timeouts (all None) so pool.get waits forever; admission acquire has no timeout; stmt_timeout wraps only the SQL statement; main.rs has no concurrency-limit or request-timeout layer. (5) Defaults match: DB_POOL_SIZE=160, QUEEN_ADMISSION_MAX=128, reserve=16 → ceiling min(128,144)=128; the reserve is purely arithmetic (admission.rs ceiling()) and reserves no actual connections from the pool-first handlers, which can drain all 160. (6) No internal recovery: in the wedge the oldest in-flight slot ages, so adapt() takes the queueing branch and shrinks the budget (never calling wake_next); growth is capped at 128 < 160; the NoSync arm pins budget 64 and doesn't wake waiters; slots release only via Slot::drop (holders stuck in pool.get) and connections only on handler completion (stuck in lane_slot) — circular wait, permanent without a restart or external client disconnects. The scenario is in fact broader than claimed: any budget value B (even the init 16) wedges once B slot-holders park on an empty pool drained by >= pool_size pool-first ack/renew/transaction/streams requests, so >=160 concurrent pool-first requests plus a saturated pop lane suffice. The reviewer's defect is real.

confirmed.title: Waiter cancellation after grant leaks inflight forever; min-budget leaks = total write outage
confirmed.failure_scenario: wake_next registers the slot (inflight incremented, entry in c.slots) and then sends the bare u64 id over the waiter's oneshot. tokio's Sender::send only fails if the receiver is already dropped; if the parked acquirer (e.g. an axum pop handler whose client disconnected, or any long-poll request future dropped by hyper) is cancelled AFTER send succeeds but BEFORE it polls rx.await (admission.rs:334), the id is silently dropped inside the dead channel: no Slot object is ever constructed, so Slot::drop never runs and the slots/inflight accounting is leaked permanently. Consequences compound: (1) the leaked entry becomes and stays the oldest slot, so adapt's queueing test (admission.rs:449, oldest_age > 4*cycle) fires on every tick and pins the budget at admission_min forever -- one single disconnect in the race window permanently degrades the broker to min budget (~15s after the leak); (2) after admission_min (default 8) accumulated leaks, total_inflight >= budget holds forever, every acquire parks forever and every try_acquire fails, i.e. no push/pop/ack/maint transaction ever commits again. Under production pop churn (thousands of grants/s, routine client disconnects while parked) this accumulates monotonically over a long-running process with no recovery path except restart. The rollback at admission.rs:383-387 only covers the receiver-dropped-before-send case; the granted-but-never-received case needs the receiver side to own a drop-guard (send a Slot, not an id).
confirmed.why: CONFIRMED on the current code. wake_next (admission.rs:384-394) registers the slot (inflight++ and c.slots insert via register, line 387) before sending a bare u64 over oneshot::Sender<u64> (Waiter.tx, line 128). tokio's send errs only if the receiver is already dropped; the rollback (389-393) covers only that case. If the parked acquire future (rx.await, line 340) is dropped after a successful send but before being polled — routine for axum/hyper long-poll pop handlers on client disconnect, and acquire(Lane::Pop) is awaited at 6 cancellable sites in handlers/data.rs — the id is dropped inside the dead channel, no Slot is constructed, and Slot::drop never runs. Grep confirms accounting is released only in Slot::drop (287-288) and the send-Err rollback (390-392); no reaper/timeout exists, so the leak is permanent. Consequences verified: the leaked non-Maint entry stays the oldest slot in the BTreeMap, making adapt's queueing test (line 458) permanently true under traffic, shrinking the budget every 500ms tick (default) to the clamp floor admission_min (default 8, config.rs:675) with no growth path — one disconnect in the window degrades the broker to min budget in roughly the claimed ~15s. After 8 accumulated leaks total_inflight >= budget holds forever: try_acquire always fails, wake_next's guard (line 368) never admits, acquire parks forever on all lanes (all write paths funnel through this one arbiter), i.e., total write outage with restart as the only recovery. Only nit: cited line numbers are off by a few lines (send at 388 not 382, rx.await at 340 not 334), which does not affect the verdict. The fix direction (receiver-owned drop-guard: send a Slot, not an id) is correct.

confirmed.title: Maint lane starves unboundedly when budget < 20: retention/stats/spool-drain stall
confirmed.failure_scenario: wake_next's guaranteed share is floor(budget * share): with the default maint share 0.05 the guarantee is 0 for any budget < 20, and the default admission_min is 8 -- exactly where AIMD parks the budget under sustained WAL pressure (and where findings on retention/leak pin it). With guarantee 0, `inflight < guaranteed` (0 < 0) is never true for Maint, so Maint waiters are only served by the fallback at admission.rs:373-376, which is strict priority Ack > Pop > Push > Maint with no aging. Under sustained saturation (the exact regime this arbiter targets) there is a continuous stream of ack/pop/push waiters, so at every wake instant some higher lane is picked and the Maint waiter is never popped. All four Maint acquirers block inside their periodic loop bodies with no timeout: retention.rs:241 (retention never prunes -> unbounded disk/partition growth), stats.rs:94 (stats table goes stale), syscollect.rs:64, and file_buffer.rs:661 (spool drain -- buffered recovery pushes are never replayed to PG while live traffic saturates, indefinitely deferring durability of already-accepted messages).

Every load-bearing fact in the claim matches the code; nothing refutes it.

confirmed.title: wake_next grant/cancel race leaks an inflight slot forever and then pins the budget at min
confirmed.failure_scenario: wake_next pre-registers the slot (inflight++, slots.insert) and then does w.tx.send(id); the rollback only runs when send() ERRORS. But tokio oneshot send() succeeds whenever the Receiver is still alive, even if it is never polled again. Sequence: (1) a pop handler is parked in acquire() at rx.await; (2) another task drops a Slot, wake_next locks core, registers id N and send(id) returns Ok; (3) the HTTP client disconnects and axum drops the handler future before it polls rx — the Receiver is dropped with the id buried inside, no Slot struct is ever constructed, so Slot::drop never runs. inflight[lane] and the slots BTreeMap entry for id N leak permanently. Double damage: (a) one budget unit is gone for the life of the process (repeated leaks walk the effective budget to zero); (b) the leaked entry is the immortal oldest slot, so adapt()'s oldest_age (line 439-449) grows without bound, `queueing` is true on every tick, and the budget is ratcheted to cfg.min and stays there forever — a single leaked waiter permanently degrades the whole broker. Client-disconnect-while-queued is precisely the saturation scenario in which waiters exist, so this fires in production over hours. The retired vegas.rs did not have this bug: tokio::sync::Semaphore returns permits when an AcquireFuture is cancelled. Fix shape: send the constructed Slot through the oneshot (a Slot dropped inside the dead channel runs Drop and releases), instead of sending a bare id.
confirmed.why: CONFIRMED on current code. wake_next (admission.rs:384-394) registers the slot (inflight++, slots.insert) then sends the bare id over a tokio oneshot; rollback only runs when send() Errs, but send() returns Ok whenever the Receiver is alive even if never polled again. A pop long-poll handler parked at rx.await in acquire() (lines 340-349) is an axum handler future (handlers/data.rs:614/774/1152/1344 call acquire(Lane::Pop) directly, no spawn) that hyper drops on client disconnect with no lock synchronizing against the granter, so the interleaving send-Ok -> future-dropped-before-poll is reachable; the id is a bare u64 buried in the dead channel, no Slot is constructed, and grep confirms Slot::drop (287-288) plus the send-Err rollback (390-392) are the ONLY sites that remove slots entries or decrement inflight — no sweeper exists, so the leak is permanent. Damage (a) holds: total_inflight stays elevated forever, eating one budget unit per leak. Damage (b) holds: slots is a BTreeMap keyed by increasing id, so the leaked non-Maint entry becomes the first values() hit in adapt()'s oldest_age (448-453); its age grows unboundedly, queueing (line 458) is true every tick under traffic, the shrink branch beats growth unconditionally, and budget clamps to cfg.min permanently. Side claims verified: vegas.rs deleted vs c2abd32; tokio Semaphore returns permits on cancelled acquire. Minor non-rescuing caveats: NoSync mode pins budget to nosync_budget instead of min, and with zero traffic the adapter holds — (a) stands regardless.

confirmed.title: db.rs metered wrappers acquire admission while already holding a pooled connection: lock-order inversion, unbounded circular wait
confirmed.failure_scenario: Every other converted site takes slot FIRST, then pool.get (data.rs:614/774/1152/1344/1664/1815, pop_fusion.rs:285→296, ack_fusion.rs:322→343, fusion.rs:623→1095, stats.rs, file_buffer.rs, retention.rs). The six db.rs wrappers (ack_at:175, ack_by_hash:231, seg_dlq_head:267, renew_lease:529, transaction:551, streams_cycle:1821) invert this: their callers check out the client before calling (data.rs:2500 uses client.as_ref().unwrap(), data.rs:2614, data.rs:2860, data.rs:2982, data.rs:3535, streams.rs:346-350), then the wrapper blocks in lane_slot(). create_pool (db.rs:11, PoolConfig::new) leaves deadpool's wait timeout at None, so pool.get waits forever. Deadlock: budget B (ceiling 128 at defaults) fully held by slot-first pop/push tasks blocked in pool.get(); all 160 connections held by concurrent renew/sync-ack/transaction/streams handlers blocked in lane_slot(Ack/Push) because inflight >= budget. No slot ever drops (its holder needs a connection), no connection ever returns (its holder needs a slot) — permanent broker-wide stall with no timeout escape. Reachable with ack-fusion off or under renew storms (thousands of leased consumers exist on the bench rigs). Even short of the full cycle, connections parked in lane_slot() silently consume the pool_reserve the ceiling() invariant (admission.rs:119-124) assumes is free for unmetered work.
confirmed.why: Verified adversarially on the working tree (diff vs c2abd32). Every factual element of the claim holds: (1) the six db.rs wrappers (ack_at:175, ack_by_hash:231, seg_dlq_head:267, renew_lease:529, transaction:551, streams_cycle:1821) all receive an already-checked-out pooled client from their callers (data.rs:2397→2500/2614/2860, 2970→2982, 3321→3535, streams.rs:346→350) and then block in lane_slot() — connection-then-slot; (2) every other metered site is slot-then-connection and holds the Slot across pool.get (data.rs:614/774/1152/1344/1664/1815, pop_fusion.rs:285→296, ack_fusion.rs:322→343, fusion.rs:626→1095, stats.rs:94→96, file_buffer.rs:661→665, retention.rs:241→242); (3) create_pool uses PoolConfig::new which per vendored deadpool 0.12.3 leaves wait timeout None, so pool.get waits forever; Admission::acquire has no timeout and the global arbiter is installed (main.rs:114); (4) defaults give ceiling 128 vs pool 160 as claimed; (5) the adapter cannot rescue: in a stall the 10s train window empties, cycle() returns None and adapt() holds forever, and the oldest-age signal shrinks rather than grows; (6) pool_reserve is accounting-only in ceiling() — nothing reserves real connections, so conn-holding lane_slot waiters do consume the reserve, confirming the secondary claim too. This is the classic two-semaphore opposite-order circular wait: all budget slots held by slot-first tasks blocked in pool.get, all connections held by conn-first wrapper callers blocked in lane_slot, no timeout on either side, absorbing state with no code-level escape. Reachable under renew/sync-ack/transaction bursts (fusion off, or the always-synchronous renew/transaction/streams paths) on rigs with thousands of leased consumers. confirmed.title: commit_done fed on empty (no-write) pop claims at all six data.rs sites, violating the module contract and poisoning NoSync detection and train clustering
confirmed.failure_scenario: admission.rs:52-53 documents the contract: a slot dropped on a pool failure or an EMPTY TAKE 'contributes no fake train sample'. But all six converted sites gate on `matches!(res, Ok(Ok(_)))` (data.rs:637, 794, 1173, 1442, 1687, 1838), which is true for any successful SQL round trip including one that claimed zero messages — the has_pending superset race, a stale targeted hint (pop_specific), a hotlist candidate lost to a concurrent consumer, or an empty partition/discover poll iteration. An empty claim is a read-only commit with no WAL flush wait, so: (a) its RTT can land under NOSYNC_FLOOR=200us (indexed empty probe on a local socket), and one such sample in the 10s rtts window makes rtt_floor < floor, flipping the adapter to Mode::NoSync (admission.rs:414-429) — budget pinned to the static nosync_budget and adaptation disabled on a fully synchronous-commit system, with Normal/NoSync flapping as samples age out; (b) empty-poll completions arrive at poll cadence rather than flush cadence, so TrainStats::feed merges real trains across the inter-flush gap (any completion within train_gap=300us of the last extends cur_last) or fabricates trains, corrupting cycle_p50/cycle_min and thus both the inflation-shrink and the saturated-grow decisions. pop_fusion.rs:355 has the same hole one level up: `outcome.is_ok() && !rtt.is_zero()` still feeds a fused flush whose every claim came back empty (an empty BEGIN..COMMIT with no writes). The gate should be 'claimed at least one message', not 'SQL returned Ok'.
confirmed.why: CONFIRMED in substance (with bounded overstatements). Verified on the working tree vs c2abd32: (1) all six data.rs sites (637, 794, 1173, 1442, 1687, 1838) gate commit_done on matches!(res, Ok(Ok(_))) — these lines replaced the old pop_vegas.record in the refactor — and pop_fusion.rs:355-357 gates on outcome.is_ok() && !rtt.is_zero(); an empty claim returns Ok (empty JSON, and even error-shaped JSON payloads ride Ok), so zero-claim SQL successes do feed the train sensor at every cited site. (2) The poisoning mechanics are real in the code: rtt_floor() is the 10s-window MIN (admission.rs:227-229), so ONE sample under NOSYNC_FLOOR=200us (line 93) flips Mode::NoSync (lines 420-435), pins the budget to nosync_budget, disables adaptation, and flaps as samples age out; TrainStats::feed (lines 145-181) extends/merges trains on any completion within train_gap (default 300us, config.rs:678), and cycle() (187-208) drives both the shrink (inflation) and grow (saturated) AIMD decisions from train-start gaps — so flush-uncorrelated completions genuinely corrupt them. (3) Genuinely read-only (no XID, no flush wait) empty claims reach these feeds in realistic operation: the has_pending superset race, stale targeted hints landing on a leased row (the FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED at 004_log_pop.sql:233-244 finds nothing and takes no lock), hotlist candidates lost to a concurrent consumer, pops on a not-yet-created partition (v_pid NULL immediate return — consumer-starts-before-producer, the cheapest probe and most plausible sub-200us sample), window-debounce returns, and parked discover re-polls inside the SP's 30s watermark throttle; handle_pop_partition and handle_pop_discover have no has_pending gate, so parked loops feed every backoff iteration. The module doc (admission.rs:51-53 "empty take ... contributes no fake train sample"; sensor defined over "write completions" and "commit rtt samples") supports the reviewer's contract reading in substance. Caveats that bound severity but do not overturn: (a) the claim's blanket premise "an empty claim is a read-only commit with no WAL flush wait" is wrong for the single most common empty case — a parked poll on an existing caught-up partition locks the log_consumers row FOR UPDATE, which assigns an XID and WAL-logs the tuple lock, so its commit DOES wait on the flush and is a legitimate flush-cadence sample (the SQL comment "parked long-polls stay read-only" refers only to the segments probe), and the empty-partition cursor seal (004:368-375) even UPDATEs; (b) the NoSync flip requires an actual sub-200us SQL wall — plausible for the v_pid-NULL/leased-skip probes on a local socket but contradicted as routine by the repo's own ~1ms empty-targeted-pop note (data.rs:797-798), so scenario (a) is environment-dependent while scenario (b) (train merge/fabrication from poll-cadence read-only feeds) holds unconditionally whenever such empties coincide with real traffic. Net: the gate is provably 'SQL returned Ok' where the sensor's documented model requires a write-commit completion; the defect and at least the train-corruption consequence genuinely hold on the current code.

(1) Mechanism: wake_next (server/src/admission.rs:384-394) registers the slot into c.slots/c.inflight via register() at line 387, then sends a bare u64 over a tokio oneshot at line 388; the rollback only handles send Err, but tokio oneshot send errs only if the Receiver was ALREADY dropped — if the receiver is dropped after a successful send, the buffered u64 is silently discarded and, having no Drop, releases nothing. confirmed.title: Empty pop results feed commit_done, flipping the arbiter into spurious NoSync mode
confirmed.failure_scenario: All six direct pop sites gate the sensor on matches!(res, Ok(Ok(_))) (data.rs:637, 794, 1173, 1442, 1687, 1838), which includes SQL calls that claimed nothing. pop_specific/pop_discover re-polls (no has_pending gate, unlike handle_pop:608) run a read-only transaction — no WAL flush — and on a local/fast rig complete in under 200µs. rtt_floor() is the MIN over the 10s window (admission.rs:226-228), so a single such sample makes floor < NOSYNC_FLOOR (200µs, admission.rs:93) and adapt() flips to Mode::NoSync (admission.rs:420-434), pinning the budget at the static nosync_budget (default 64) on a fully durable system and disabling the adaptive control; mode then flaps as the window rotates past the sample. On a 2-core cell where the adaptive budget would sit near 8-16, a pinned 64 concurrent write txns recreates exactly the WAL overload this refactor was built to prevent. Violates the module's own contract that commit_done marks 'a real commit completion' (admission.rs:257-259).

confirmed.title: Maint lane starves indefinitely at sustained saturation: retention stops, spool replay can't drain

Conversely, when retention DOES run it holds one of the floor-8 slots for the entire multi-second stepped cycle — a sustained 12.5% budget tax at min that the old code never levied.

1. Caveat: B is not guaranteed to stay pinned at exactly 8 forever — the cycle floor is a rolling 10s p25, so steady (non-worsening) inflation eventually reads as flat and saturation grows B by ~ln(B) per 500ms tick; if B ever reaches 20, Maint gets a guaranteed slot of 1 and starvation becomes bounded. All four call sites verified, all blocking with no timeout wrapper: retention.rs:241 (acquired at the top of run_cycle, before pool.get(); run_loop at retention.rs:141-150 is a single sequential loop, so a blocked acquire stops retention entirely — no segment/txn purge), stats.rs:94, syscollect.rs:64, and file_buffer.rs:661 (replay_batch, the spool drain — deliberately Maint-lane "recovery traffic must never outrank live lanes", so post-outage replay cannot drain while recovering clients keep ack/pop/push waiters queued).

confirmed.title: Cycle gap conflates arrival cadence with flush-cycle duration: load downshift reads as cycle-inflation and collapses the budget to min
confirmed.failure_scenario: At low utilization each commit is its own train, so the gap between train starts is INTER-ARRIVAL time, not the flush interval. Recovery is saturation-gated ln-additive growth: min back to 128 needs ~28 ticks = 14s of throttled admission. Any periodic burst/lull producer (cron jobs every few seconds, phased bench runs) keeps the arbiter permanently oscillating at min: every lull shrinks, every burst starts throttled. Shrink on cycle-inflation needs a utilization/saturation gate (only shrink when the budget was actually the binding constraint) or the floor/p50 comparison must exclude idle-cadence gaps.

confirmed.title: NoSync detection uses window-MIN of commit rtts: a single fast sample pins the static budget; idle latches the mode
